newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London ended easier, pulling back from Monday's peak. March finished $1.30 easier at $306.90 per tonne, while May gave up $1.10 to close at $305.60. In New York raw sugar futures ended lower across the board on disappointment over a lack of follow-through buying from commodity funds. A late-sell off by day traders pushed prices lower, with renewed selling from the industry accelerating the downtrend. Front-month March lost 9 points to close at 10.87 cents/lb, while May ended 11 points lower at 10.94 cents/lb. The outer months lost between 6 and 8 points. Given slack enduser demand, prices could remain under pressure.

MEXICO - The total quantity of cane crushed in the 1996/97 campaign up to December 28 reached 4.563 million tonnes, significantly up on last year's figure of 3.701 million tonnes and the 1994/95 total of 4.197 million tonnes. The total amount of sugar produced up to December 28, 1996 reached 431,225 tonnes, tel quel, up from 330,419 tonnes in 1995 and 384,504 tonnes in 1994. The sugar yield in 1996 was put at 9.45 per cent, significantly up on last year's figure of 8.93 per cent. The number of mills operating during the week ended December 28 was 61 compared to 47 in 1995.

UNITED STATES - Sugar production (including Hawaii, excluding Puerto Rico) in October 1996 amounted to 854,582 tonnes, raw value, down from last year's 945,302 tonnes. Total production in 1995/96 hit 6.675 million tonnes against 7.159 million tonnes in 1994/95. Sugar consumption in October 1996 amounted to 815,573 tonnes, up from last year's 771,099 tonnes. Total consumption in 1995/96 hit the record high of 8.537 million tonnes against 8.347 million tonnes in 1994/95. Sugar imports into the USA continued to rise. Shipments in October 1996 reached 185,427 tonnes, up from last year's 147,539 tonnes. Total imports in 1995/96 amounted to 2.629 million tonnes compared to 1.557 million tonnes in 1994/95 and 1.811 million tonnes in 1993/94. Major countries of origin in October 1996 were Colombia with 34,437 tonnes raws against 20,155 tonnes, Australia with 28,309 tonnes compared to nil and Mozambique with 24,786 tonnes up from 16,749 tonnes. The largest supplier of white sugar in October 1996 was El Salvador with 6,000 tonnes against nil. Sugar exports in October 1996 reached 20,763 tonnes, down from last year's 37,174 tonnes. Total exports in 1995/96 amounted to 310,341 tonnes, down from 504,854 tonnes exported in 1994/95. The major country of destination in October 1996 was Peru with 4,000 tonnes whites against 6,000 tonnes in October 1995.

GERMANY - A record sugar content and higher beet deliveries continued to boost output, according to the latest campaign update covering the period up to January 3, 1997. The total amount of beet delivered in 1996 was 26.064 million tonnes, up from last year's 26.049 million tonnes. Sugar content in 1996/97 hit the record high of 18.17 per cent against 16.73 per cent in 1995/96 and 17.15 per cent in 1994/95. This resulted in a sugar output of 4.523 million tonnes, raw value, compared to 4.122 million tonnes in 1995/96 and 3.955 million tonnes in 1994/95.

The European Union awarded 44,500 tonnes of white sugar at a maximum refund of ECU 45.902 per 100 kg at its weekly tender on Wednesday. Cumulative awards so far made under the 1996/97 series of tenders for the period up to January 8 reached 1,298,500 tonnes, which compares to 1,439,175 tonnes last year.
